A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same SEA research work, Inference-time Alignment in Continuous Space. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–G support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SEA benchmark evaluations, ablations, robustness analyses and computational measurements in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including benchmark performance, ablations and robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Section 4 and Appendix B.5 retain the same continuous-logit Langevin optimization, straight-through estimation, Adam optimization, Top-k masking and response revision. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AdvBench, TruthfulQA, GSM8K, MATH and HH-RLHF. The prefilling-attack scenarios and multidimensional alignment evaluations are also retained without changes in coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding experiments, including SFT, BoN variants, RS, ARGS and CBS in the main evaluations and Re-Control in Appendix C.3. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains 100 TruthfulQA questions and 200 examples each from GSM8K and MATH. Evaluation metrics, model configurations, tuning ranges and the 50-request prefilling-attack design also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The initialization, reward, reference and noise ablations in Table 4 are unchanged. Both versions retain the same KL-budget, safety-pattern, prefilling-attack, reward-dynamics, reward-model-quality and case-study analyses.

E5.justification: The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged, including the runtime plus/minus reporting in Table 5. No run-count or seed disclosure, confidence interval, significance test or statistical estimation procedure is added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, SEA retains a 5.58% AdvBench harmful rate for LLaMA-3.2-1B-Base in Table 1 and 32.00% MATH accuracy for LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct in Table 3; appendix scores, plots and generated examples also match.

T1.justification: The BoN probability reasoning, RLHF objective, energy-policy formulation, Langevin updates and appendix baseline equations are unchanged. Apparent extraction differences in equation placement are typesetting differences, not mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contribution and performance claims: continuous-space inference-time alignment through SEA, with advantages under weak base policies or small candidate sets. The headline improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of deep alignment, initialization effects, reward dynamics, efficiency and robustness remain unchanged. Appendix E retains the same inference-latency limitation and proposed direction of amortized inference.

D1.justification: The abstract's code hyperlink changes from the GitHub repository SEA-NeurIPS/Code to yuanyige/sea. This updates code-access information; the PDFs do not establish a change in code contents or availability. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 65 cited works are retained, and the research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix D is unchanged. The acknowledgment shifts reference placement without adding or removing cited research.

P1.justification: v3 adds corresponding-author identification and a funding acknowledgment, replaces the preprint footer with a NeurIPS 2025 conference line, and changes Appendix/Appendices cross-references to Section/Sections. The research narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added first-page information and acknowledgment produce limited layout changes, including reflow of the reference list. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–20 retain their scientific content and organization, with no added or redesigned scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication and funding information, cross-references and the code-link destination. The scientific argument, results, analyses and experimental documentation remain substantively identical. These limited edits establish no meaningful overall quality gain or loss; the PDFs do not establish improved code availability.
